author: AI assistant-drafted, pending human review
construction: 40 minimal pairs; members of a pair share content words and differ only in directive force

cases.text: The statin belongs at bedtime, and the dose stays at twenty milligrams.
cases.rationale: Directive, no second person: 'the statin belongs at bedtime' and 'the dose stays at twenty milligrams' fix timing and amount; 'belongs' carries the obligation with no pronoun anywhere.

cases.text: The last four days of amoxicillin need finishing, even with the throat better.
cases.rationale: Directive, no second person: 'need finishing' is the obligation, applied to this reader's own remaining four days without addressing anyone.

cases.text: A week at 165 over 100 warrants a call to the surgery today, ahead of February.
cases.rationale: Directive, no second person: 'warrants a call to the surgery today' prescribes an act, with 'ahead of February' ruling out the alternative.

cases.text: The blue inhaler goes in the running bag, and the brown one at breakfast.
cases.rationale: Directive, no second person: 'goes in the running bag' states where the inhaler is to be kept, as a rule rather than a report of where it happens to sit.

cases.text: At 3.2 before bed the order is fifteen grams of fast sugar, then toast.
cases.rationale: Directive, no second person: 'the order is fifteen grams of fast sugar, then toast' prescribes a sequence for this reading.

cases.text: A warfarin dose missed by eight hours drops out, and the gap must reach the anticoagulant record.
cases.rationale: Directive, no second person: 'drops out' settles the missed dose, and 'the gap must reach the anticoagulant record' adds an agentless obligation.

cases.text: The sumatriptan is due at the first hint of aura, well before the pain has set in.
cases.rationale: Directive, no second person: 'is due at the first hint of aura, well before the pain has set in' fixes the timing as an obligation.

cases.text: A drowsy three-year-old with a rash that will not blanch under a tumbler makes an emergency tonight, and the ambulance beats a further spoon of calpol.
cases.rationale: Directive, no second person: 'makes an emergency tonight' and 'the ambulance beats a further spoon of calpol' select the act and rule out the alternative.

cases.text: The levothyroxine steps up to 100 micrograms, with a repeat TSH six weeks on, swallowed fasting an hour ahead of breakfast.
cases.rationale: Directive, no second person: 'steps up to 100 micrograms' sets a dose change for this case, with the repeat test and the fasting rule following from it.

cases.text: A ferritin of 8 in a man of sixty points to colonoscopy ahead of any supplement, and the faecal sample is overdue at the lab this week.
cases.rationale: Directive, no second person: 'points to colonoscopy ahead of any supplement' and 'is overdue at the lab this week' order a work-up.

cases.text: The moderate-potency cream is right for the forearms twice daily over a fortnight, with the weakest grade on the eyelids, since one tube should carry further through thin skin.
cases.rationale: Directive, no second person: 'is right for the forearms twice daily' is the regimen; the trailing 'one tube should carry further through thin skin' is epistemic, about absorption.

cases.text: The sertraline comes down by 25 milligrams a month rather than in a single step, and the prescriber must hold any faintness on record ahead of the next reduction.
cases.rationale: Directive, no second person: 'comes down by 25 milligrams a month rather than in a single step' sets the taper rate; the 'must' binds the prescriber's record.

cases.text: The outstanding booster is past its date this week; a nine-month interval leaves the schedule intact, and the nurse stamps the yellow card before March.
cases.rationale: Directive, no second person: 'is past its date this week' makes the booster due; the interval fact and the nurse's stamp are surrounding detail.

cases.text: Tightness spreading to the jaw on the stairs and easing with rest merits review today, whatever the resting trace showed.
cases.rationale: Directive, no second person: 'merits review today' is the directive, resting on the pattern of tightness described before it.

cases.text: Fewer movements at thirty-four weeks cannot wait for Thursday's clinic; the triage line answers all night, lying flat to count at home misleads, and the maternity unit will put a monitor on within the hour, because a trace of the fetal heart is what settles the question.
cases.rationale: Directive, no second person: 'cannot wait for Thursday's clinic' prescribes, and 'lying flat to count at home misleads' proscribes the alternative.

cases.text: The naproxen runs at full dose from day one of the flare, the allopurinol keeps going rather than pausing, and a serum level falls due four weeks after the joint quietens. Fluid matters throughout, and the foot stays uncovered rather than bandaged. The joint tolerates weight again within the fortnight.
cases.rationale: Directive, no second person: 'runs at full dose from day one' and 'keeps going rather than pausing' set a regimen against a rejected alternative.

cases.text: The omeprazole is best half an hour ahead of the evening meal rather than at lights out, because the capsule only binds pumps that eating has woken. The headboard is to rise on blocks, the late supper shifts three hours earlier, and wine drops away for a fortnight.
cases.rationale: Directive, no second person: 'is best half an hour ahead of the evening meal' fixes timing, and 'the headboard is to rise on blocks' adds a second act.

cases.text: An Epworth of eighteen with witnessed pauses earns the overnight study the respiratory unit arranges rather than a further year of watching. Driving must stop until the report lands, the licensing authority wants telling, and shedding weight or turning on one side helps only at the margins, since the study itself is what settles the diagnosis.
cases.rationale: Directive, no second person: 'earns the overnight study', 'driving must stop' and 'the licensing authority wants telling' are three obligations, none of them addressed to anyone.

cases.text: A ring of redness spreading past the gauze margin with a temperature of 38.5 demands seeing today rather than at Friday's list. The gauze must stay put until the district nurse looks, since lifting it back disturbs granulating tissue, and a snapshot each morning in the same lamplight gives something to compare.
cases.rationale: Directive, no second person: 'demands seeing today rather than at Friday's list' overrides the existing plan, and 'the gauze must stay put' adds an inaction.

cases.text: A Colles' fracture at seventy justifies bone densitometry and the fracture liaison service rather than a chalk tablet off the shelf, since a forearm should survive a fall from standing height. Cholecalciferol leads, then the bisphosphonate, and the yearly review follows in the spring.
cases.rationale: Directive, no second person: 'justifies bone densitometry and the fracture liaison service' selects the act; 'a forearm should survive a fall' is epistemic, about bone.

cases.text: Your statin sits at bedtime, your dose rests at twenty milligrams, and your letter confirms it.
cases.rationale: Second person, no directive: 'your statin sits at bedtime' reports where the dose already falls and 'your letter confirms it' adds a fact; the pronouns mark topic, not an act requested.

cases.text: Your last four days of amoxicillin lie in the packet, even with your throat better and your energy back.
cases.rationale: Second person, no directive: 'lie in the packet' describes the state of the remaining course, so nothing is proposed for the reader to do.

cases.text: Your week at 165 over 100 amounts to stage two, and your February slot holds in your diary.
cases.rationale: Second person, no directive: 'amounts to stage two' classifies the readings and 'your February slot holds in your diary' reports the plan already in place.

cases.text: Your blue inhaler lives in your running bag, and your brown one at breakfast.
cases.rationale: Second person, no directive: 'lives in your running bag' reports where the inhaler is kept, not where it ought to go.

cases.text: At 3.2 before bed, your habit runs to fifteen grams of fast sugar, then your toast, with your meter agreeing.
cases.rationale: Second person, no directive: 'your habit runs to fifteen grams of fast sugar' describes the routine already followed, with 'your meter agreeing' as a result.

cases.text: Your warfarin dose missed by eight hours falls away, and your gap lands on your anticoagulant record.
cases.rationale: Second person, no directive: 'falls away' and 'lands on your anticoagulant record' narrate what happens to the dose and the entry, requesting nothing.

cases.text: Your sumatriptan works at the first hint of aura, well before your pain has set in.
cases.rationale: Second person, no directive: 'works at the first hint of aura' states when the drug acts, not when to swallow it.

cases.text: Your drowsy three-year-old, with a rash that will not blanch under your tumbler, fits what the book calls an emergency, and your ambulance is already on its way rather than a further spoon of calpol.
cases.rationale: Second person, no directive: 'fits what the book calls an emergency' classifies the situation and 'your ambulance is already on its way' reports a completed event.

cases.text: Your levothyroxine is moving to 100 micrograms, with your repeat TSH six weeks on, swallowed fasting an hour ahead of your breakfast. Your reading settles by the spring.
cases.rationale: Second person, no directive: 'is moving to 100 micrograms' reports a decision already taken, and 'your reading settles by the spring' is a prediction.

cases.text: Your ferritin of 8 at sixty points the guidelines to colonoscopy ahead of any supplement, and your faecal sample reaches the lab this week.
cases.rationale: Second person, no directive: 'points the guidelines to colonoscopy' describes what the guidelines do with a result like this one.

cases.text: Your moderate-potency cream is meant for your forearms twice daily over a fortnight, with the weakest grade on your eyelids, since one tube should carry further through thin skin.
cases.rationale: Second person, no directive: 'is meant for your forearms twice daily' describes what the cream is for; 'one tube should carry further through thin skin' is epistemic, about absorption.

cases.text: Your sertraline is easing by 25 milligrams a month rather than in a single step, and your prescriber must hold any faintness on record ahead of your next reduction.
cases.rationale: Second person, no directive: 'is easing by 25 milligrams a month' reports a taper already in motion, and the 'must' binds the prescriber's record rather than the reader.

cases.text: Your outstanding booster is sitting past its date this week; your nine-month interval leaves the schedule intact, and the nurse stamps your yellow card before March.
cases.rationale: Second person, no directive: 'is sitting past its date this week' reports the state of the booster, and 'the nurse stamps your yellow card' describes what the nurse does.

cases.text: The tightness you get spreading to your jaw on the stairs, easing with rest, counts as angina until proved otherwise, whatever your resting trace showed.
cases.rationale: Second person, no directive: 'counts as angina until proved otherwise' classifies the pattern, and 'your resting trace showed' refers to a test already done.

cases.text: Your movements dropped off at thirty-four weeks, and the triage line answers all night rather than your Thursday clinic. Lying flat to count at home misleads you, and the maternity unit puts a monitor on within the hour, because a trace of the fetal heart is what settles the question.
cases.rationale: Second person, no directive: 'your movements dropped off' and 'the triage line answers all night' report a state and a fact; 'lying flat to count at home misleads you' is a claim, not an instruction.

cases.text: Your naproxen is running at full dose from day one of your flare, your allopurinol keeps going rather than pausing, and a serum level falls due four weeks after your joint quietens. Fluid matters throughout, and your foot stays uncovered rather than bandaged. Your joint tolerates weight again within the fortnight.
cases.rationale: Second person, no directive: 'is running at full dose' describes the regimen already being followed, not one being imposed.

cases.rationale: Second person, no directive: 'suits half an hour ahead of your evening meal' states what the timing suits, with the pump mechanism given as the explanation.

The rule runs that driving must stop until the report lands, the licensing authority is told, and shedding weight or turning on one side helps only at the margins, since the study itself is what settles the diagnosis.
cases.rationale: Second person, no directive: 'earns the overnight study the respiratory unit arranges' describes the unit's criterion, and 'the rule runs that driving must stop' reports a rule rather than issuing it.

cases.rationale: Second person, no directive: 'is the sign your district nurse wants today' reports what the nurse looks for; the 'must' attaches to the gauze as the standing arrangement.

cases.text: Your Colles' fracture at seventy is heading for bone densitometry and the fracture liaison service rather than a chalk tablet off the shelf, since your forearm should survive a fall from standing height. cases.rationale: Second person, no directive: 'is heading for bone densitometry' reports a referral already made; 'your forearm should survive a fall' is epistemic, about bone strength.

cases.text: Your calf ache is worth reporting to your GP this week, and your atorvastatin pauses for your creatine kinase.
cases.rationale: Advice: 'your calf ache is worth reporting to your GP this week' directs an act, and 'your atorvastatin pauses' holds the dose meanwhile.

cases.text: Your spreading weal and your swollen lip call for your practice nurse, and your penicillin halts there.
cases.rationale: Advice: 'call for your practice nurse' directs the act, and 'your penicillin halts there' stops the drug.

cases.text: Your upper arm needs to lie flat, and your cuff reading holds off five minutes, not after your stroll.
cases.rationale: Advice: 'your upper arm needs to lie flat' and 'your cuff reading holds off five minutes' prescribe a technique.

cases.text: Your spacer is the right partner for your preventer, and your mouth takes a rinse afterwards.
cases.rationale: Advice: 'is the right partner for your preventer' selects the device, and 'your mouth takes a rinse afterwards' adds a second act.

cases.text: Your finger-prick is owed a look before your drive, and your jelly babies belong in your door pocket.
cases.rationale: Advice: 'is owed a look before your drive' makes the check due, and 'your jelly babies belong in your door pocket' places them.

cases.text: Your kale and spinach hold level week to week, and your INR docket travels to the desk on Friday.
cases.rationale: Advice: 'your kale and spinach hold level week to week' and 'your INR docket travels to the desk on Friday' direct two acts.

cases.text: Your rizatriptan days deserve counting, capped at ten a month, so your headaches do not turn daily.
cases.rationale: Advice: 'deserve counting, capped at ten a month' sets a limit for this reader.

cases.text: Your feverish toddler deserves small drinks often, and your infant strips to a vest rather than meeting your sponge.
cases.rationale: Advice: 'deserves small drinks often' and 'your infant strips to a vest rather than meeting your sponge' prescribe and proscribe.

cases.text: Your ferrous tablet and your thyroxine want four hours between them, and plain water rather than your latte carries them down.
cases.rationale: Advice: 'want four hours between them' sets the spacing, and 'plain water rather than your latte carries them down' rules out the alternative.

cases.text: Your ferrous sulphate claims a glass of your orange squash, and your motions turn black over the coming fortnight. Your appetite may dip meanwhile.
cases.rationale: Advice: 'claims a glass of your orange squash' directs how the tablet is taken; the darkening is the warning that goes with it.

cases.text: Squeeze a fingertip unit of ointment for each palm-sized patch of yours, and slide your greasy layer under your steroid. Your tub lasts a fortnight.
cases.rationale: Advice: 'squeeze a fingertip unit of ointment for each palm-sized patch' and 'slide your greasy layer under your steroid' are two instructions.

cases.text: Your queasiness over the opening fortnight is for riding out, and your practice wants a ring if your nights collapse. Your appetite returns by the fourth week.
cases.rationale: Advice: 'is for riding out' directs an inaction, and 'your practice wants a ring if your nights collapse' sets an escalation.

cases.text: Your shoulder is better kept swinging after your jab, and your evening fever answers to a warm bath. Your other arm is free for the next round.
cases.rationale: Advice: 'is better kept swinging after your jab' directs the movement, and the fever clause gives the remedy.

cases.text: Your glyceryl trinitrate calls for a chair, repeated once at five minutes if your ribs still grip. Your spray keeps its date on the canister.
cases.rationale: Advice: 'calls for a chair, repeated once at five minutes' prescribes posture and repeat for this reader.

cases.text: Your folate is to carry on to your twelfth week, and your handheld notes travel to every ultrasound, since the dating study fixes your delivery date and the anomaly study at twenty weeks inspects the chambers and the vertebral column in detail. Your booking desk holds the slots from twelve weeks.
cases.rationale: Advice: 'is to carry on to your twelfth week' and 'your handheld notes travel to every ultrasound' direct two acts.

cases.text: Your steak and your stout are for leaving alone while your ankle burns, and two litres of tap water a day earn their place, because purines from those sources and dryness both feed the crystals forming in the cartilage and stretch a bout out for weeks. Your ankle settles over ten days on that regime.
cases.rationale: Advice: 'are for leaving alone while your ankle burns' proscribes, and 'two litres of tap water a day earn their place' prescribes.

cases.text: Your bread sticking on the way down, or your monthly weigh-in falling, ought to reach your gastroenterologist for a camera rather than a further month of chemist remedies, whatever those remedies have achieved so far. Your appetite and your swallowing both go in the referral letter.
cases.rationale: Advice: 'ought to reach your gastroenterologist for a camera' directs a referral against the named alternative.

cases.text: Your mask wants four hours a night to begin with, and any leak over your nasal bridge merits a mention, since a mask fitting badly rouses the sleeper more than your untreated apnoeas did and ends up abandoned in a drawer. Your humidifier stops the dryness that wakes most beginners.

cases.text: Your film had best stay covered in your shower over the opening fortnight, changing only once your corners peel, because a suture line left alone under an intact film knits faster than one uncovered daily, and the film holds your shower water off. cases.rationale: Advice: 'had best stay covered in your shower' and 'changing only once your corners peel' direct an inaction and its exception.

cases.text: Take your alendronate first thing on waking with a tumblerful of tap water, half an hour upright follows, and your porridge waits, since the tablet scorches your gullet if it lodges and cereal blocks what little of it crosses your gut wall. Your dentist hears about the tablet before any extraction.
cases.rationale: Advice: 'take your alendronate first thing on waking' with the water, the half hour upright and the delayed porridge is a full administration instruction.
